notes: One-year token mint takes a grant back from the host that refreshes it. Ten Claude accounts were handed to the box (Refreshed by → box) before Convert all existed, and on the Mac both "Replace with a one-year token" and "Convert all to one-year tokens" refused every one of those rows with "the grant is refreshed by another host (env_…); convert it there", which nobody can do on a headless box. Now staticTokens.ts mint() runs the new AccountSync.takeBack first for a row another host refreshes: the existing takeOver pull accounts.setHome uses (the grant lands provisionally, accounts.confirm with the refresh fingerprint, the owner strips to an access copy), then the refresh route mints from the grant as for a local one, the static profile has no owner and syncs to every host. A host out of reach, or one that keeps the grant, leaves the stored claude.ai session and then the sign-in window to mint (the order T1 built), and when those fail too the row's reason names the host and what happened here ("B, which refreshes the grant, is not connected; the stored claude.ai session has lapsed"), never the other host's UI. Convert all walks the same per row with its progress. Tests: staticTokens.test.ts (13: a reachable owner's grant taken back and minted; an owner out of reach falls through to the session; the row message when the session and the sign-in fail too), accountSync.test.ts (15: takeBack over a fake link, the kept and the disconnected answers). Proof: scripts/e2e-static-tokens.ts now 35 checks, with `four`, a grant B refreshes and A holds an access copy of: Convert all on A pulls it back (B hands out and strips on the confirm), mints it with no consent page, B lands the token; nothing owned remains for the account on either host and B's live sign-in is untouched. CLAUDE.md and docs/box.md say so.
